content.title: FOOD FACTS THAT SOUND MADE UP BUT ARE 100% REAL
facts: **Nutmeg** contains a natural compound called myristicin that, in large enough doses, causes hallucinations — a teaspoon or two eaten at once has sent people to the ER thinking they took a drug.
**Cashews** are never sold in their raw shell to consumers because the shell contains a resin closely related to poison ivy's — the nuts you eat have already been steam-treated to remove it.
**Rhubarb** leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely toxic, while the stalks right next to them are perfectly safe and turned into pie for generations.

**Nutritional yeast** is a living organism (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) that's deliberately deactivated with heat — it's the same species used to brew beer and bake bread, just grown for its B-vitamin content instead.

**Star fruit** contains a neurotoxin that healthy kidneys filter out easily, but in people with kidney disease it can cause hiccups, confusion, and seizures — a fruit doctors actually warn dialysis patients away from.
**Cinnamon** sticks are literally rolled tree bark — the spice jar in your cabinet is dried, curled bark from the Cinnamomum tree, harvested the same way for over 2,000 years.
**Black pepper** was once so valuable it was used as currency to pay rent and dowries in medieval Europe, earning the nickname 'black gold.'

content.caption:
The nutmeg fact still gets people every time — myristicin is metabolized in your liver into a compound structurally similar to amphetamines, which is why more than a teaspoon or two can cause real hallucinations and a racing heart, not just a spicy pie. Cashews are a great one too: that toxic shell resin (urushiol) is destroyed through steam or roasting before the nuts ever leave the processing facility, which is also why you'll never find a 'raw cashew in shell' at the store — it's not marketing, it's safety. And star fruit is a genuinely underrated warning: the neurotoxin caramboxin is normally cleared by your kidneys within hours, but if kidney function is impaired it builds up in the bloodstream and can cross into the brain. Everyone's body handles things differently, so when in doubt, check with a doctor about anything you're unsure of.
